lore_snippet: A damp, lawless shanty-market built over glowing marshes, thick with heavy violet mists where traders peddle illicit goods and narcotics like red honey.

display_name: The Albion to Eleutheria Transit Relay
lore_snippet: There is a certain homemade quality to the transit relay at Duskings Deep. The buildings are cottagey, the sequencer-wheels are under constant repair, and the customs procedures are lax. But it is the most direct route to Eleutheria.

display_name: The Albion Transit Relay to the Reach
lore_snippet: The London end of the Avid Horizon transit, tightly monitored by Admiralty officials overseeing locomotives venturing into the verdant wilderness of the Reach. This one leads to the Reach: a sunless wilderness, rich in opportunity and peril, coveted by London.

A stone edifice, scintillant with sigils, is encased in a contrivance of steel and brass. This is a Singh-Jenkins relay, allowing transport across the sunless wastes to Albion: the heart of the new British Empire and the seat of Her Renewed Majesty Queen Victoria.
A quiet wash of flowers in the dark—fields of asphodel where shadows worn to weariness find gentle rest.
In this place that is two places, the void turns blindingly pale and the high sky shudders with memories of the Unterzee.
A terrifying, solemn archway surrounded by azure light and glacial silence, pointing toward the domain of the dead and the Sapphir'd King.

display_name: The Blue Kingdom's Transit Relay to the Reach
lore_snippet: The Kingdom's only transit relay was built by London's embassy, then yielded to the local authorities. Now, its rooms hang with silks of blue and gold. Pale petals carpet the floors. There is no need to pay for passage. Instead, the Inhabitor-of-the-Threshold will determine whether you are permitted to leave. It is served by the spirits of jackals, which lounge lazily in the corridors until someone seeks passage.
A massive, soot-blackened, free-floating industrial factory complex where the Empire's debtors and lower classes are relentlessly ground away to manufacture mass cargo.
Miners burrowed too deep into this worldlet, unearthing a violent, chittering disgruntlement of Cantankeri from the stone.
A military platform occupied by an army of rogue devils who have turned their backs on hell to wage an endless war of their own design.
Known as the Grave of Roses, this is a beautiful, stone-pillared sanctuary where civilized devils tend to quiet gardens and gather cosmic secrets.
A quiet, eerie penitentiary overseen by devils who offer the penitent a chance to refine, alter, or completely scrub away their sins.
London's monumental, artificial substitute for a dead Judgement, bathing the inner reaches of Albion in a sickly, mechanical gold light that threatens to drive onlookers mad.
The sun! The sun! THESUNTHESUNTHESUN! An artificial, gold-creamed glare throbbing against the glass with blinding, mind-shattering heat.
The bureaucratic heart and regional headquarters of the Windward Company, representing London's stark imperial interests in the Reach.
The still-cooling corpse of the King of Hours shudders far below, its fires dead and blackened to mark Her Majesty's bloody victory.
A bleak, deafening station where the dead are processed, sorted, and sent down deep trenches to tunnel toward their final metaphysical progression.
Bleak, forgotten cyclopean ruins where glowing correspondence sigils crawl along fractured stone like marching ants.
A black and seething star turned to night! When the gaze of the Halved turns upon the bridge, the crew wails as its impossible eye fills the glass.
The proud, neon-lit capital of the Eagle Khanate. Independent from London, it burns brightly in the deep darkness under the glow of their artificial moon.

A frost-rimed iron gateway facing the dark vastness of Eleutheria, where the rules of London weaken and the night claims all horizon. This one leads to Eleutheria: a place of revolutionaries and malcontents. It is little used.

display_name: The Eleutherian Transit Relay to Albion
lore_snippet: The recently-constructed relay to Albion is ramshackle and fortified. Gaunt, rifle-toting guards watch for stirrings in the dark. The sigils of the sequencer-wheels coat everything in sullen red.

display_name: The Eleutherian Transit Relay to the Reach
lore_snippet: An imposing black-iron bastion drifting in the eternal night of Eleutheria, regulating transit back to the overgrown frontier of the Reach.
The titanic, rotting remains of a celestial Messenger resting in the dark—a fallen behemoth of heaven that brings tears to watching eyes.
The Westminster government buildings, meticulously relocated from the subterranean Neath to the stars, only to be cast out to the windy fringes of Albion by Her Majesty.
An immense, blinding industrial forge choked with gleaming white dust, where human spirits are fundamentally broken down, purified, or reforged.
A suspicious, highly elite club house platform facilitating backroom deals, smugglers, and the distribution of forbidden materials.
HIC SVNT DRACONES inscribed across an ancient tomb; the crew flies softly on muffled throttle, whispering that even death may die.
A quiet, predatory platform drifting near Pan, covered in sprawling alien flora engineered to ensnare careless skyfarers.
The grand, frozen gateway through which London originally migrated into the High Wilderness; it is now shut fast, chillingly quiet, and heavily guarded.
The cosmic dial by which the silent servants of the Sapphir'd King govern every ritual, observance, and transit in the kingdom of the dead.
The radiant, overwhelming court of the Sun's Daughter, where souls can attempt to petition the cosmic bureaucracy of the Pansekritis.

display_name: The House of Rods and Chains
lore_snippet: A ruined complex built directly upon the carcass of a massive, dead celestial Messenger that disobeyed the ancient judgment of the suns.
A verdant, fungal settlement nestled within dense vegetation whose original colonists mysteriously vanished without a trace.
A surreal, isolated estate lit by London-style lamp-posts, where an aristocratic lord lives out eccentric eccentricities amidst an untrustworthy staff.
A corporate sanctuary established to study and domesticate the wild, overgrown flora and fauna native to the High Wilderness.
The smog-choked, industrial powerhouse capital of the British Empire-in-Exile, ruled over by Her Renewed Majesty from the Throne of Hours.
A freezing, ramshackle frontier town built around the Mother of Mountains where desperate prospectors mine frozen time.
A sanctuary for those seeking treatment, recovery, or comfortable concealment from the psychological burdens of the sky.
A small, solemn stone raised to the brave rattus faber who perished in the early exodus to Heaven; one by one, the crew remove their hats.
The bureaucratic extension of the crown anchored directly to London, processing the endless administrative taxes, censorship laws, and legal manifests of the Empire.
A quiet, hauntingly beautiful necropolis of drifting stone tombs, where Londoners inter their deceased amidst the soft chime of mourning gears.
The bustling cosmopolitan hub of the Reach, caught in a perpetual, simmering tug-of-war between London Loyalists and Tackety Rebels.
A lightless, terrifying throat gaping in the western sky like an open wound, sighing with the cold void of an unstitched grave.
The wild, divided, and lawless central hub of Eleutheria, governed by the enigmatic Cypress King where storytelling is explicitly a crime.
A beautiful, crystalline resort caught in a localized, engineered pocket of permanent time, where London's high society lives beautifully and endlessly without aging.
An architectural prison without doors or visible cells, where inmates wander beautiful, twisting mazes of stone, gradually losing their identities.
A dazzling, bizarre traveling entertainment troupe operating out of giant tents strung between drifting space rocks.
A sleepy, picturesque riverside community modeled directly after rural Britain, masking deep-rooted traditional superstitions.
A heavily fortified corporate stronghold acting as the primary military bastion and gateway for London's nobility into the Reach.
Near the quiet heart of the shifting wood, a silent, solemn clearing where cold dread gathers thick beneath the boughs.
A tremble in the air swells into thunder as crystalline falls tumble through the sky, alight with all the hues of heaven.
The premier academic citadel of the High Wilderness, where eccentric scientists and state-sanctioned researchers explore dangerous frontiers of cosmic anatomy.
The broken remnants of a grand astronomical foundation, once kissed by the light of a long-dead Judgement.
A structural spire sitting under the gaze of the dead Judgement, holding the vaults and offices of the realm's rigid Arbiters.
London's fragile bureaucratic outpost established in the kingdom of the dead; it is the single port where living skyfarers outnumber the deceased.
Old, cold ruins standing in a deliberate ring like strokes on a clockface, enveloped by the frayed threads of unravelling time.
A slender grey pillar watching over the misty sea, casting a queasy, piercing beam that cuts through the fog like a drowned needle.
A colossal, plunging infrastructure that descends away into the lightless deeps, serving as a bleak checkpoint for those staring into Albion's watery underbelly.
Looming, shattered masonry where lambent, unreadable sigils cast an eerie, sickly glow through the curling mists.
An ambitious settlement constructed entirely inside a giant, hollowed-out mechanical sky-flower, vulnerable to the elements.
A fallen giant suspended in the mist—the very Biggest of Bens, whose rare, echoing chimes promise good luck to all aboard.
An ancient, labyrinthine, and inherently hostile forest of moving trees that harbors dangerous secrets of the Garden-King.
The rowdy political meeting hall and temporary capital of the Tackety Independence movement, sitting in defiance of London rule.
A lightless gravitational wound in the celestial wild where the frozen void sighs with ancient, ravenous cold.
A shimmering tear in reality where colors unknown to earthly eyes bleed into the perpetual night.
A high-security prison platform anchored directly to the lips of the White Well, used to hold and punish the erroneous dead before their final sentences.
A terrifying, deep cosmic drain where celestial judgement is pronounced and the condemned are cast into lightless, absolute erasure.
A cold, structural platform resting in the orbit of Pan, used by seasonal outcasts waiting out political shifts within the region.
An expansive processing platform connected to the London core, converting massive timber hauls into structural locomotive components.
A charming yet eerie seaside resort town cloaked in fog, where tourists walk boardwalks and play midway games over a sky that mimics an ocean.
A homemade moon forged at the Khan's decree, its vast steel lattice festooned with burning lamps that stain the velvet dark with warm, yellow light.
